content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 68.0+ values), then underestimates the subsequent decline.
- Tends to underestimate the true mean of the 30-day window, particularly in the middle-to-late period.
- Shows persistent lag in recognizing downward momentum; often delays correction after a peak.
- Overreacts to recent volatility, producing exaggerated peaks in forecast when true price stabilizes.
- Underestimates the true long-term trend (last 10–15 days) — model flattens too early, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts too aggressively revert to prior levels, missing sustained drift.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days.
